To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of a temperature-elevated chromatographic separation with online-coupling to a continuous-flow enzyme-assay allows the detection of enzyme-regulatory effects in complex mixtures.

the online coupling of chromatographic separation with continuous-flow enzymatic assay can be a powerful tool for the investigation of enzyme-regulatory effects of complex mixtures, and that the method is especially useful for the identification and characterization of unknown features.

a chromatographic Perilla extract separation coupled to a temperature-controlled xanthine oxidize assay was developed and successfully used for the identification of unknown compounds as well as for the observation of an enzyme inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a chromatography-assisted online enzymatic assay.
the development of a chromatographic system for the online-couple of chromatographic Per. frutescensextract separation with an enzyme assay.
the online-coupled HPLC-enzymatic assay method for the separation of P. frutesces extract and the detection of its enzymatic activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presented online-coupling method allows the detection of enzyme-regulatory compounds in complex mixtures, but that further optimization of the method is required to allow for the identification of unknown compounds.
the method is suitable for the online-couple of HPLC and enzyme assay, and can be used to identify the active compounds in complex mixtures.
a chromatography-based method was developed and applied to investigate the enzymatic effects of P. frutescen extracts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the online-coupled HPLC-enzyme assay is a useful tool for screening of complex mixtures, and the method is applicable for the study of natural extracts.

we have established an efficient and reliable HPLC method for the separation of P. frutesces extract, which can be used for the identification of unknown components and the investigation of the effect of P. fructescens extract on the enzyme xanthine oxidoreductase.
the method developed can be applied to the analysis of complex plant extracts and the online-coupled enzymatic assay can be used for the investigation of enzyme-inhibitory compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a chromatographic system with a moderate temperature gradient can be used for a fast and efficient separation of plant extracts.
the method developed can be applied for the analysis of complex plant extracts and the determination of their effects on enzymatic activity.
the developed chromatographic conditions are suitable for the online coupling of chromatographic separation with an enzymatic assay.
